searches.note: Twelve searches for Bollinger and ten for Ayala: twenty two of a share of twenty four for the two pilots, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Six were restricted to champagne-bollinger.com and read through their summaries. No WebFetch was tried.

method: The record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the founders, Lily Bollinger and her dates, the village, the kind of producer, the dated changes, the grapes and shares, the villages by vintage, the name and first vintage of La Grande Année, the lees, the dosage, the forms, R.D. and Vieilles Vignes Françaises, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries; the forty five second lines were counted inside 90 to 110 words by the lint.
The record was set beside the published flagships record (key bollinger, refuted on 12 November 2026), the library's p-bollinger and the Champagne region record; nothing there was edited.

tested.founded: 6 February 1829, Renaudin-Bollinger and Cie, three partners, the Count of Villermont kept from trade as an aristocrat, Paul Renaudin at the cellar and Joseph Bollinger at the sales: the house's own history page and the Union. 1829 agrees with the library and the flagships record. Württemberg is the published record's, not found again on the house's page, and stands as published.
tested.story: The Royal Warrant of 1884 from Queen Victoria: the house. Lily Bollinger (1899 to 1977), at the head from 1941 to 1971 after her husband's death: Wikipedia and the Irish Times, with Decanter; the bicycle is the published record's. R.D. launched in 1967 with the 1952 vintage: the house's R.D. page and Decanter; no source of 1961 found. Vieilles Vignes Françaises first made in 1969: Decanter and Tastingbook; three ungrafted plots until Croix Rouge in Bouzy gave its last fruit to the 2004 vintage: Decanter, the wine anorak's visit and a merchant. Grande Année from the 1976 vintage: Decanter and Tastingbook, against one merchant's club that lists Millésime to 1982 and Grande Année from 1983. Ayala bought in January 2005: the Union's chronology.
tested.kind: NM was searched for on a label and not found.
tested.style: Special Cuvée: 60 per cent Pinot Noir, 25 Chardonnay, 15 Meunier, over 85 per cent Grand and Premier Cru, a majority of reserve wines with some in magnum for 7 to 15 years, 7 to 8 grams, twice the appellation's ageing: the house's page; the importer's sheets give about half reserve, 5 to 15 years in magnum and 8 to 9 grams, and another house page 5 to 15 years. The reserve magnums are documented at the house since 1890, by the house.
tested.cuvee: 2015: 11 crus, Pinot Noir 60 per cent of Verzenay, Aÿ and Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, Chardonnay 40 of Chouilly and Avize, 8 grams, 8 to 10 degrees. 2018: 19 crus, Pinot Noir 66 per cent of Verzenay, Aÿ and Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, Chardonnay of Chouilly and Cuis, 6 grams, 10 to 12 degrees. Rosé 2014: 19 crus, Chouilly and Oiry; Rosé 2015 with red wine of La Côte aux Enfants. All by the house's pages. The house's page for the cuvée speaks of ten years of patience in the cellars, which the record's more than twice three years does not contradict.
tested.table: The six spoken lines read aloud: opened by hand in cuvee45 read as the cork drawn at the table and is now cleared of its sediment by hand; the white Burgundy of the sale had no source and is the published table line's main course.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read; one right answer each, wrong options of the sheet's houses or of Bollinger's own dates, no length clue. Fronts and stems unchanged, so every id holds; the second question's explanation now says up to fifteen years.

changes.was: and in 1969 made the first Vieilles Vignes Françaises, from two small plots of ungrafted Pinot Noir in Aÿ.
changes.now: and in 1969 made the first Vieilles Vignes Françaises, from ungrafted Pinot Noir; a third plot, in Bouzy, gave its last fruit to the 2004 vintage, leaving two walled plots in Aÿ.
changes.why: Until 2004 a third ungrafted plot, Croix Rouge in Bouzy, went into the wine; the two Aÿ plots alone hold from the 2005 vintage.
sources: Decanter: Bollinger Vieilles Vignes Françaises, a rare prestige cuvée
Wine Anorak: Visiting Champagne Bollinger, part 1

changes.was: took the name Grande Année with the 1976 vintage.
changes.now: took the name Grande Année with the 1976 vintage, by most accounts.
changes.why: Decanter and Tastingbook say 1976; one merchant's club lists Grande Année from 1983.

changes.now: some of them kept in magnum under cork, for 7 to 15 years by that page and 5 to 15 by another.
changes.why: The house's Special Cuvée page says 7 to 15 years, its Special Cuvée 007 page and the importer 5 to 15.

changes.was: keeps reserve wines in magnum under cork for 7 to 15 years.
changes.now: keeps part of its reserve wines in magnum under cork for up to fifteen years.
changes.why: The same finding; part of them, as the published record has it.

open: NM was not read on a label; it rests on the Union des Maisons de Champagne listing the house and on the definition.
Malolactic conversion: not stated on any page read.
The name Grande Année: 1976 by Decanter and Tastingbook, 1983 by one merchant's club; the house's pages read do not date it.
Special Cuvée's dosage and reserve: 7 to 8 grams and a majority of reserve wines by the house, 8 to 9 grams and about half by its importer's sheets; the record follows the house.
codexInTension: Producers and flagships, bollinger: others gives Vieilles Vignes Françaises as from two small plots of ungrafted Pinot Noir in Aÿ, first made in 1969, and the story calls the two plots inside Aÿ its source; the wine drew on a third plot, Croix Rouge in Bouzy, until the 2004 vintage, so the two plots hold from the 2005 vintage on. Listed for the owner; the published record is not changed here.

Producers and flagships, bollinger: sites says about twenty Grand and Premier Cru villages; the house gives 19 crus for the 2014 and 2018 vintages and 11 for the 2015. A refinement by vintage, not a contradiction.

Producers and flagships, bollinger: serve says 9 to 11 degrees Celsius; the house's pages give 8 to 10 for the 2014 and 2015 and 10 to 12 for the 2018. The record keeps the published range and gives the house's beside it.

The Champagne region record says Bollinger is partly fermented in old oak, while every base wine of La Grande Année ferments in oak by the house; the region line speaks of the house as a whole, so no contradiction is claimed.
